whatWeProvide.title: Two supply lines, one accountable partner
whatWeProvide.lead: Hospital-grade consumables for institutional procurement, and cross-border access to medicines that aren't yet available in your market — run through the same sourcing, documentation, and logistics discipline.

items.title: Hospital Supplies
items.desc: IV and infusion therapy, blood bank and transfusion products, surgical connectivity, airway management, and medical gas — verified, specification-documented consumables for institutional procurement.

items.title: Specialty Medicines
items.desc: Named-patient and cross-border access to oncology therapies, rare biosimilars, and critical-care medicines that aren't yet registered or available in your market, with cold-chain-monitored delivery.

items.title: Sourcing, Logistics & Trade
items.desc: A dual-hub sourcing and fulfillment network connecting India's manufacturing base and Southeast Asia's logistics corridor to hospitals, distributors, and manufacturer partners worldwide.

whoWeHelp.title: Built for institutional procurement and specialist access
whoWeHelp.lead: Four groups rely on us for the requirements that standard distribution does not cover — each with its own intake route, documentation set, and point of contact.

items.title: Hospitals & Procurement Teams
items.desc: Specification-documented consumables quoted against your tender line list, with certification references attached, so wards and theatres are never held up waiting on a missing item.

items.title: Clinicians & Oncology Teams
items.desc: Named-patient and cross-border access to therapies not yet registered in your market, supported by the manufacturer documentation your pharmacy committee and regulator will ask to see.

items.title: Distributors & Manufacturer Partners
items.desc: Cross-border reach into markets that are difficult to serve directly, through a two-hub network built for sourcing, consolidation, and onward distribution.

items.title: Patients & Families

howItWorks.title: Two workflows, one accountable team
howItWorks.lead: Institutional procurement and named-patient access follow different rules, different documentation, and different timelines. We run them as separate tracks so neither slows the other down.

tracks.name: Hospital Procurement
tracks.summary: For facilities, procurement officers, and tender teams sourcing medical-surgical consumables at volume.

steps.title: Requirement
steps.desc: You send a requirement or tender line list — product, specification, volume, destination. No login or account required.

steps.title: Quotation & Specification
steps.desc: We return a quote line by line, with the product specifications and certification references attached to each item.

steps.title: Order & Documentation
steps.desc: On approval we confirm the order and compile the documentation pack your procurement, pharmacy, and regulatory reviewers need.

steps.title: Consolidated Fulfilment
steps.desc: Dispatch from our India sourcing hub or Philippines logistics hub, consolidated where possible and cold-chain controlled where the product requires it.

tracks.name: Specialty & Named-Patient Access
tracks.summary: For treating physicians and hospital pharmacies sourcing a medicine that is not registered or not available locally.

steps.title: Clinical Request
steps.desc: The treating physician submits the product, strength, quantity, and patient context for a named-patient requisition.

steps.title: Sourcing & Verification
steps.desc: We source from verified manufacturers and assemble the Certificates of Analysis and manufacturing credentials for clinical and regulatory review.

steps.title: Regulatory Pathway
steps.desc: We support the import permit and named-patient documentation required by the destination market, working to the prescriber's timeline.

steps.title: Cold-Chain Delivery
steps.desc: Temperature-monitored shipment direct to the treating facility, with the chain of custody documented from dispatch to handover.

qualityCompliance.responseCommitment: Every institutional requisition and specialty-access request is reviewed by a named case manager, with a response inside 24 hours. No login required to request a quote.

questions.q: What does named-patient supply actually mean?
questions.a: If a medicine is not registered or not available in your market, the named-patient pathway lets a treating physician request it for one identified patient. We source the product from a verified manufacturer and support the import permit and documentation the destination regulator requires.

questions.q: What documentation comes with a quote?
questions.a: Product specifications and the certification references that apply to each line — CE marking and CMDR approvals for devices, WHO-GMP credentials and Certificates of Analysis for pharmaceuticals, and ISO 9809-1 / DOT/TPED certification for gas cylinders. Documentation varies by product and destination market, so we state it line by line rather than as a blanket claim.

questions.q: Do we need an account or login to request a quote?
questions.a: No. Institutional requisitions and specialty-access requests are submitted directly through the contact workflow, and a case manager responds within 24 hours.

questions.q: How do you handle cold-chain products?
questions.a: Temperature-sensitive products ship in monitored packaging, with the temperature record and chain of custody documented from dispatch through to handover at the treating facility.

questions.q: Where do you source from, and where do you deliver?
questions.a: Sourcing runs through our India hub in New Delhi and logistics through our Philippines hub in Metro Manila, serving hospitals, clinics, and trade partners across more than 50 countries.

questions.q: What are your minimum order quantities and lead times?
questions.a: Both depend on the product category, volume, and destination market, so we confirm them on the quote rather than publishing a single figure. Send your line list and we will come back with quantities, lead times, and documentation together.

questions.q: Can you support tenders and framework agreements?
questions.a: Yes. Send the tender line list or framework schedule and we will quote against the stated specifications, flagging any line where an equivalent product or an alternative certification route is the better fit.
